name: Jeff Nippard Powerbuilding System
author: Jeff Nippard
structure: Full-body and upper/lower weeks in turn. Main lifts take a heavy top set; accessories cover 1-5, 6-12 and 12-20 reps.
progression: Percentages mixed with RPE. A paid programme: its rules were not available to check.
adapt: Runs on percentages and RPE targets that change by week, which the app does not have. Nothing beyond the product page is known about it.
caveats: Paid. Some users find its estimated maxes conservative. Only its existence and outline are confirmed.

name: Kizen 16 Week Powerbuilding
author: Silent Mike, Bart Kwan, Omar Isuf
structure: Three barbell days (one of high reps, one heavy, one moderate) alternating with three days of superset accessories.
progression: In the four weeks that are public the percentages rise about 2.5 % a week, up to about 77.5 %.
adapt: Loads are percentages that rise weekly, which the app does not have; and only the first four of its sixteen weeks are public.
caveats: A popular powerbuilding programme. Six days is a high bar, and the public weeks are too light to prepare for a meet.

name: Brogains Powerbuilding
author: Brogan Pratt
structure: Upper and lower days, each as a heavy day and a dynamic day; close to PHUL in shape, and usable as a peak before a meet.
progression: Percentages with a peak. The rules were not checked.
adapt: Runs on percentages the app does not have, and its details are not known.
caveats: Little material to go on. Only its existence and outline are confirmed.

name: Westside for Skinny Bastards (Part 3)
author: Joe DeFranco
level: late novice to intermediate, written for athletes
structure: Monday upper-body max effort, working up to a 3-5 rep max; Tuesday lower-body dynamic work with jumps and single-leg lifts; Thursday upper-body repetition day at 3x15; Friday lower-body max effort.
progression: The max-effort lift changes every two weeks and each time has to beat the last, by reps first and then load. Accessories work up to 20 reps a set, then add 2.5 kg (5 lb) and return to 15. No deload is planned.
adapt: The plan holds an exercise until it is changed, so the two-week rotation of the max-effort lift is a swap made at a review; between reviews the lift stays. Run it on `double` over 3-5 reps. Jumps are logged as bodyweight work.
caveats: Balanced pushing and pulling and plenty of single-side work. Each main lift gets one top set, so volume is low.
